correctness.rationale: The proof reduces odd-cycle frustration to a simplex of nonnegative phase errors of total pi, since strictly decreasing cosine on [0,pi] forces minimal total absolute error. Pairwise cos averaging uniquely equalizes the k=n-1 strong errors; maximizing B_w(delta)=k cos(delta)-w cos(k delta) on [0,pi/k] and monotonic sin(k delta)/sin(delta) prove exactly one collinear minimizing class at and below 1/k, exactly two reflection-paired noncollinear classes above. Taylor expansion verifies the stated current sqrt coefficient, quartic threshold and quadratic energy-gap coefficient; the quotient Hessian is positive at nonthreshold minima and Euler multipliers become stable for sufficiently small h. The argument is all odd n>=5, not extrapolated from the finite numerical script. Independently optimized representative n,w examples and checked exact critical coefficients.
